newsitem.title: CANADA: Southam shrs anticipate upped Hollinger bid.
newsitem.headline: Southam shrs anticipate upped Hollinger bid.

text.p: Shares in Southam Inc rose in busy trading on Tuesday, fueled by expectations that Hollinger Inc's Conrad Black would have to sweeten his C$23.50 a share bid to take Southam private.

Analysts said recent published comments by major Southam shareholders that the offer for the newspaper chain was not rich enough would likely spur Black to increase the C$923 million bid for the Southam shares he did not already own.
"I think there's more value in Southam to be had... I think there's a good chance we'll see an improvement to the bid," one analyst said.
Southam rose 0.30 to 22.80 on almost 340,000 shares by midday today.

Some minority shareholders have said the bid should be at least C$25 a share. The offer included C$13.50 a share in cash and a C$10 non-voting special share in Hollinger Canadian, a unit of Hollinger International Inc.

Hollinger officials were unavailable for comment on Tuesday, but Black told Hollinger's annual meeting on May 27 that he would consider increasing the cash portion of the offer but not the bid's overall value.
The analyst said there was no telling which way Black would go to raise the bid.
"It's hard to say. It could be one or both, price or the mix of paper and cash," she said.
Under Southam rules, Black's offer would fail if it was rejected by at least 33.33 percent of minority shareholders.
Toronto-based Hollinger owns 50.4 percent of Southam shares.

Southam's independent directors were expected to make a recommendation to shareholders on the bid as early as today. In November, the committee compelled Black to increase an previous offer for seven million shares by C$1.25 a share to C$20. That deal gave Black control of the Southam chain.
